subject: Optimize Toolkit packaging & pilot pricing — quant/cache guidance
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@fincomp.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-13T09:12:45-08:00
Subject: Initial questions — Optimize toolkit packaging for FinComp pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A few follow-ups from the product and procurement teams as we think about a 3-month pilot moving to production:

- Can you outline the packaging options for the Optimize toolkit (credits vs committed tokens vs slab tiers)?
- We're particularly interested in batching/KV cache recommendations for a mixed workload: 60% short chat prompts (~16 tokens avg) and 40% longer summarization/embedding flows (~800 tokens avg). Any quantization advice you have (FP16 vs int8) and the expected impact on latency/quality would be helpful.
- What sort of pilot discounts or credits do you typically provide, and how do you handle SLA uplift during pilot vs production?

I've attached a short procurement Qs PDF for context. Procurement is looped as procurement@fincomp.ai — they'd like an outline we can share internally before a pricing call.

Can we do a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow?

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform
FinComp AI

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@fincomp.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-13T15:04:10-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions — Optimize toolkit packaging for FinComp pilot

Elena — great talking earlier. High level answers first, we can flesh out numbers on a call: 

1) Packaging options (short):
- Pilot credits: time-limited token pool applied to the account (best for fast evals).
- Committed monthly spend: predictable throughput, slab discounts as usage bands increase.
- Flexpath: smaller commit + overage credits that are tiered — useful for bursty workloads.

2) Batching + KV cache recommendation for your workload:
- Start cache-first for long flows: persist KV cache for summarization sessions and reuse across requests — expect a 25–40% effective token reduction on long-run summarization/embedding flows if sessions have reuse.
- Continuous batching on short prompts: configure small, aggressive batching windows (10–30ms) to preserve latency while improving GPU utilization.

3) Quantization:
- We recommend an evaluation: int8 quantization is often a sweet spot for throughput/cost with modest quality delta on most transformer families; FP16 is safest quality-wise but less cost-reduction.
- For generation quality-sensitive routes (customer-facing summaries), run a parallel AB test: FP16 baseline vs int8 candidate on your eval prompts.

4) Pilot discounts / SLA:
- Typical pilot: 3 months with pilot credits + a pilot discount (we'll propose ranges). SLA uplift is available as an add-on during production; pilot SLAs are lower by default but we can provide tighter SLOs for a short-term fee.

I'll attach a one-pager and a simple pricing scenarios workbook for you. Can do a call tomorrow 10:00 PT or Friday morning.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: optimize-toolkit-one-pager.pdf, pricing-scenarios.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-11-14T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial questions — packaging + pilot pricing (internal)

Irene / Vanessa — quick internal note after reading Elena's procurement doc and our one-pager:

- Proposal idea (for discussion before we present):
  * Pilot: 3 months, 100k token/day pilot credit pool (equates to ~9M tokens total) + 20% pilot discount on any overage. We price pilot to allow a real evaluation and protect runway.
  * Production starter: committed monthly 1.5M tokens/month with slab discounts: 10% at 5M, 18% at 15M, 25% at 50M.
  * SLA uplift: +2% of monthly committed spend for 99.9% availability and 95th percentile latency guarantees.

- Commercial levers we can offer: one-time onboarding credit, extended pilot to 4 months if they sign PO within 30 days, and early termination protections.

- Technical recommendation: require a short quantization/quality eval during pilot. If int8 shows acceptable quality, we recommend moving to int8 for non-sensitive routes and keep FP16 for high-sensitivity generation. Note: int8 may improve throughput ~1.8–2.4x depending on model and produce ~35% lower cost per token when combined with cache/batching.

Thoughts? I can draft numbers for the call.

—Karthik
Head, Inference Product

Attachment: pricing-scenarios.xlsx (internal workbook)

Subject: Re: Initial questions — Optimize toolkit packaging for FinComp pilot

Elena / team — thanks for the note and context. We've pulled together two concrete commercial options and a short MAP (mutual action plan) below. Attaching the MAP and sample SLA for legal.

Option A — Pilot-first (recommended to validate quant/caching):
- Pilot: 3-month pilot, 9M token credit pool (≈100k tokens/day).
- Pilot economic concession: equivalent to a 25% effective discount on usage during the first 3 months (direct credits applied).
- Overages during pilot billed at list with 20% pilot overage discount.
- Technical guardrail: run int8 evaluation during month 1; if int8 meets quality thresholds agreed on the eval set, move non-sensitive routes to int8 in production.

Option B — Accelerated ramp (for faster production value):
- Pilot credits: 6M token pool (shorter runway).
- Intro production concession: 25% discount for first 3 months post-conversion, stepping to 15% for months 4–6.
- SLA uplift option: +2% fee on committed monthly amount for 99.9% availability and 95th percentile latency SLOs.

Notes on quant + cache impact (our operational estimate for your workload):
- Cache-first on long sessions: expected token reduction 30–40% on summarization/embedding flows where session reuse occurs.
- Combined with batching and int8: overall cost-per-effective-output reduction expected 30–45% vs no-cache/FP16 baseline. We will run a short eval during pilot and provide an ops playbook (how to configure TTL, shard size, and batching windows) as part of onboarding.

Mutual action plan (high level):
1) Sign pilot SOW + PO (we'll produce DocuSign).
2) Kickoff + data/eval prompt set delivery (FinComp provides canonical prompts).
3) Run quantization & cache eval (2–3 weeks).
4) Review results, choose production quant profile, and finalize committed band.
5) Production cutover + SLA activation.

Next steps: I'm available for a pricing call Wednesday 11/20 10:00 PT. If procurement wants to fast-track, we can prepare a single-sheet commercial offer with exact dollar figures and a DocuSign SOW ahead of the call.

Links / attachments: mutual-action-plan.md, sample-sla.pdf. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234/deal/FC-2024-4839.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
